outcomes.original: Filing step: File for a Limited Live Performance permit with the San Francisco Entertainment Commission. What to say: Apply online through the Entertainment Commission portal. Describe the limited live performance (one or two musicians, small performance area of 200 sq ft or less, ending by 10 p.m. or 11 p.m. as allowed by Planning Code § 719). State that the restaurant is an existing bona fide eating place with an active ABC Type 47 license, and that live music is secondary to the meal service. Submit the $612 application fee (FY2026–27). Post the yellow notice at the site for 30 days and conduct neighbor outreach before the Commission hearing. The application will be referred to the Police Department and Planning Department for review; respond promptly to any questions. Emphasize that the bar next door at 1807 Haight St was approved for outdoor entertainment in June 2024, and that this proposal is smaller in scope (indoor performance only, shorter hours).

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit a Public Health plan check for the tenant improvements (limited cooking) to the Department of Public Health. What to say: File through the DPH portal with the Business Account Number (BAN), menu, and two sets of scaled drawings showing equipment, finishes, and hand sinks. State that the restaurant is an existing operation with a limited-cooking setup (no major hood changes), and that the improvements are to add outdoor seating and refresh the interior. Pay the plan-check fee ($828 for a small remodel, 3 hours review time, or higher if the work is more extensive). Coordinate the DPH plan check with the building permit application so both departments review concurrently. After DPH approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks in advance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for a building permit with the Department of Building Inspection for the tenant improvements and outdoor seating structure. What to say: Submit plans stamped by a licensed architect showing the interior tenant improvements and the outdoor seating area (including any structure, fencing, heating, lighting). Route the application to Planning for zoning review under PC § 175(a); Planning will confirm that the use is permitted and that the outdoor area complies with the Letter of Determination. Route to DPH for concurrent plan check. Pay the building permit fee (a percentage of construction valuation, typically $800–$15,000 for tenant improvements). If the outdoor structure encroaches on required yards or alters the building footprint, address Planning and DBI comments before issuance. Obtain separate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits as needed for the work.
outcomes.note: Record covers general building permits for tenant improvements but does not mention outdoor seating, Planning routing under PC § 175(a), or Letter of Determination compliance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File for a health permit to operate with the Department of Public Health after the final DPH inspection passes. What to say: Apply online with the BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal EIN at least one month before the target opening date. Confirm that a certified food safety manager is on staff (required under CalCode § 113947.1). Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (includes the initial inspection). Schedule the final pre-opening inspection after the building permit work is complete and the space matches the DPH-approved plans. The permit is issued after the inspection passes; you cannot serve the public before it is issued.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If exterior business signage is planned, file for a sign permit with SF Planning and DBI. What to say: Submit drawings of the proposed sign (size, illumination, materials, mounting method) to Planning for review under the Haight Street NCD sign controls. Pay the sign permit fee (about $300–$1,500 depending on size and illumination). State that the restaurant is an existing use and the sign is a refresh or replacement. Planning will issue a sign permit approval; DBI issues the final permit. If the building is in a historic district or is Article 10/11 designated, the sign review will take longer.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 75 to 265 days. Estimated government cost: $1,910 to $19,412. Notes: The day and cost ranges are for the approvals granted: Conditional Use Authorization (if needed), Limited Live Performance permit, Health permit to operate, and Building permit. The minimum (75 days, $1,910) assumes no CUA is required, the LLP permit takes 30 days (filed May 21, decided June 10 = 20 days for the comparable next door), the health plan check and building permit run concurrently for 21–60 days, and the health permit issues in 14 days after the final inspection. The maximum (265 days, $19,412) assumes a CUA is required (120–300 days per the catalog, using 180 days as a midpoint based on the 2007 outdoor dining CUA that took 128 days), the LLP permit takes 60 days, the building permit takes 120 days (due to plan revisions), and the health permit takes 45 days. The cost minimum sums the LLP fee ($612), health plan check ($828), health permit ($470), and building permit minimum ($800 for a small TI, though fees rise with construction cost). The maximum assumes a CUA fee of $3,150 (estimated for 2026–27 from the 2023–24 schedule), LLP $900, health plan check $2,500, health permit $1,000, building permit $15,000, and a sign permit $1,500. These are government filing fees only; they exclude professional services (architect, expediter, lawyer), construction costs, music licensing (ASCAP/BMI ~$600–$5,000 annually), and state business setup (entity, EIN, seller's permit, workers' comp, food safety certs, RBS training). If the outdoor area requires a CUA, that hearing is the critical path and adds 4–10 months; obtain the Letter of Determination immediately to know which timeline applies.
